title: He, She, We, and the One Who
label: ch:gu-pronouns-and-relative
canDo: I can talk about somebody who is not present, choose between the two words for we, and describe a person instead of naming them.

payoff.summary: The absent third person, the two we, and the relative. te covers he, she and it with one word; ame and aapne are the exclusive and inclusive we, where choosing wrongly audibly shuts the listener out; and je ... te ... turns out to be the same two-ended shape as jo ... to ... from the chapter before -- one habit, three uses.
payoff.note: The relative takes a track-local concept rather than the canonical RELATIVE-CLAUSE, which the spine stages at B2. What is taught here is the A1 use the inventory names -- the one who -- not the full relative system.
